title: Finite-pullback identities
statement:
Finite pullback of sections, in the sense of
[def-weil-pbc-finite-section-pullback], satisfies the following four
equations: identity pullback fixes a section; pullback along a composite
equals the composite pullback; pullback commutes with restriction to the
closed fiber; and a section descended from a finite surjective refinement
pulls back to the chosen local section on that refinement.

proof.text:
The first three equations are the functoriality of the inverse-image unit of
[def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], applied to the identities $V\times_YY=V$, to
composites, and to the cartesian square defining the closed fiber of
[def-weil-pbc-finite-section-pullback]. The fourth is the uniqueness
statement in finite descent, applied to the local sections selected on the
refinement.

blueprint_update.statement:
The pullback of global sections [def-weil-pbc-finite-section-pullback]
satisfies the following four identities, for an etale sheaf $G$ on $T$ and a
commutative square $u\circ a=i\circ b$ with $a:Z'\to T'$, $b:Z'\to Z$,
$u:T'\to T$, $i:Z\to T$:

1. pullback along $\mathrm{id}_T$, followed by $\mathrm{id}_T^{-1}G\cong G$, is
   the identity of $\Gamma(T,G)$;
2. pullback along the composite $u\circ a$, followed by the composition
   isomorphism $(ua)^{-1}G\cong a^{-1}u^{-1}G$, equals $a^\sharp\circ u^\sharp$;
3. pullback commutes with restriction to the closed fibre:
   $\Gamma(\theta)\circ b^\sharp\circ i^\sharp=a^\sharp\circ u^\sharp$, where
   $\theta:b^{-1}i^{-1}G\cong a^{-1}u^{-1}G$ is the square isomorphism;
4. descended sections are preserved: if $x\in\Gamma(T,G)$ and
   $x'\in\Gamma(T',u^{-1}G)$ satisfy $u^\sharp(x)=x'$, then
   $a^\sharp(x')=\Gamma(\theta)(b^\sharp(i^\sharp(x)))$.

proof.text:
The first three equations are the functoriality of the inverse-image unit of
[def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], applied to the identity $T\times_TT=T$, to
composites, and to the two equal composites $u\circ a=i\circ b$ (the square
isomorphism being the composite of the two composition isomorphisms). The
fourth follows from the third by substituting $x'=u^\sharp(x)$.
